waterHammerLead: Simulate backflow and see when the meter can register an extra pulse.
waterHammerDiagram: Pipe layout with a water meter and solenoid valve.
waterHammerRestart: First pulse after an interrupted fill
waterHammerNote0: Illustrative example. Backflow depends on the conditions in the installation.
waterHammerNote1: When the solenoid valve closes suddenly, the moving water slows down. Pressure rises upstream of the valve, sending a pressure wave back towards the meter. This is an example of water hammer. Depending on the installation, the water can briefly flow backwards and move the needle back past the pulse threshold.
waterHammerNote2: When the valve opens again, the needle can cross the same threshold a second time in the forward direction. The meter shown here emits another pulse even though less than the nominal volume per pulse has passed.
waterHammerNote3: The display compares the volume calculated from pulses with the net volume since the last reset. The net volume accounts for water that passed backwards through the meter.
waterHammerNote4: After stopping a fill, Reset clears the pulse count and the needle stays where it is. If the needle has stopped between pulse thresholds, it only needs to travel the remaining part of a turn after restarting. The first pulse can therefore occur after less than the nominal volume has passed. This depends on the needle position at reset and can happen without backflow.
waterHammerNote5: At 1 litre per pulse, if the needle is a quarter-turn away from the threshold, the first pulse occurs after 0.25 litres. At that moment the display shows 1 l from pulses and 0.25 l net through the meter. With uninterrupted forward flow, one full nominal portion passes between subsequent pulses.
